comment: Open-data source registry for the NarcoScope pipeline. automation: 'auto' = fetched and transformed by run.mjs with no credentials; 'api-key' = automatable once a free key is configured; 'manual' = one download or copy step per release cycle, then the listed converter handles it.

sources.cadence: annual (June, with each WDR edition — bump the URL year)
sources.feeds: src/data/prices.ts (Street Prices tab)

sources.cadence: annual (June — bump the URL year and filename)

Corridor paths that remain: INCB Precursors annex tables, UNODC Synthetic Drugs SEA report, or higher-tier DMP access (dmp.unodc.org User Registration — needs an account, route dashboards are tier-gated).

sources.feeds: NOT YET INTEGRATED — candidate context layer (criminality/resilience scores beside seizure data)

sources._section: DEMAND-SIDE MODALITIES — independent of interdiction agencies. Everything above this line is collected by the same kind of body (customs, police, drug-control agencies) and therefore shares an enforcement-capacity bias. The sources below are collected by vital-statistics registrars and environmental chemists, which is what makes them able to corroborate or contradict the supply picture. See src/lib/triangulate.ts.

sources.name: CDC NCHS VSRR Provisional Drug Overdose Death Counts
sources.license: US Government work — public domain (17 U.S.C. §105)
sources.feeds: src/data/overdose.json — the mortality modality on the Triangulation tab. US national + 50 states + DC + NYC, by ICD-10 substance class, 12-month-ending windows, 2015-present.
sources.notes: Provisional: recent windows are incomplete (percentComplete carried per record). Suppressed cells are dropped, never zero-filled. T43.6 'psychostimulants' is a class code, NOT a synonym for methamphetamine — the substitution is made explicitly and reversibly in triangulate.ts's DRUG_BRIDGE, never at ingest.

sources.name: CDC WONDER — final multiple-cause-of-death mortality
sources.feeds: NOT YET INTEGRATED — final counts to replace VSRR provisional figures once a year closes. VSRR is the better default (monthly, current); WONDER is the authoritative back-series.
sources.transform: TODO — WONDER's API is an XML POST with a session-scoped request document; simpler to export CSV and run it through parseOverdoseDeaths().

sources.name: Statistics Canada — Drug metabolites in wastewater in select Canadian cities
sources.format: csv (zipped, via the keyless StatCan WDS REST API)
sources.license: Statistics Canada Open Licence — reproduction and distribution permitted with attribution
sources.feeds: src/data/wastewater.json — the wastewater modality on the Triangulation tab. 82 records, 8 cities, 2019/2020/2022/2023, cocaine + methamphetamine + cannabis (+ heroin for 2019-2020 only).
sources.notes: THE ROUTE IN, after EUDA and ACIC both proved unautomatable. Reports the SCORE standard unit directly. The two tables use different measure names AND different unit labels for the same quantity (grams per million people per day vs milligrams per thousand people per day — dimensionally identical, no conversion applied); a converter written against only the newer vocabulary silently yields zero records for the older one. Cocaine uses benzoylecgonine, never parent cocaine. Heroin uses 6-MAM and exists only in the older table. Validation case: Canadian cannabis 2019->2023 shows seizures -94% against wastewater +69%, i.e. the post-legalisation collapse in ENFORCEMENT correctly not read as a collapse in consumption.

sources.name: EUDA (ex-EMCDDA) / SCORE municipal wastewater drug loads
sources.feeds: wastewaterRecords via the CSV loader — EUROPEAN coverage for the Triangulation tab. NOTHING IS BUNDLED: re-verified 2026-07-26 that euda.europa.eu returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients on both the current and legacy data URLs, including the copy linked from data.europa.eu, so this cannot be automated. The bundled default is statcan-wastewater (Canada); loading a verified EUDA export extends divergence detection to Europe.
sources.notes: Unit must be mg per 1,000 inhabitants per day (the SCORE standard). Wastewater is the only modality here that measures consumption directly — blind to enforcement effort, reporting willingness, and mortality.

sources.name: ACIC National Wastewater Drug Monitoring Programme (Australia)
sources.feeds: wastewaterRecords via the CSV loader. Methodologically the most rigorous wastewater programme in the world (national coverage, consistent catchments, long series). data.gov.au carries no machine-readable release as of 2026-07-26.

sources._section: OFFICIAL DESIGNATIONS — published government actions naming entities under a stated legal authority. Distinct in kind from the investigative-report sources below, which publish allegations. That distinction is why designations are bundled as data and reports are not.

sources.name: US Treasury OFAC — Specially Designated Nationals list
sources.license: US Government work — public domain (17 U.S.C. §105)
sources.feeds: src/data/designations.json — the Designations tab. Filtered to SDNTK (Kingpin Act), SDNT, ILLICIT-DRUGS-EO14059 (fentanyl authority) and TCO (transnational criminal organisations).
sources.notes: Fetched from Treasury DIRECTLY rather than via OpenSanctions: public domain with no licence condition, which is the only footing on which this can ship in an MIT repo. alt.csv gives OFAC's own alias equivalences, which solves the transliteration-variant entity-resolution problem with published ground truth instead of inference. Addresses, passport/ID numbers and dates of birth are present upstream and deliberately NOT extracted.

sources.name: UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List
sources.feeds: EVALUATED 2026-07-27, NOT INTEGRATED: the list is reachable (2.2 MB, 736 individuals + 275 entities) but it is a counter-terrorism / non-proliferation instrument, NOT a narcotics one. Zero opium/meth/fentanyl entries; only 12 entities mention drug trafficking at all, and all 12 are Taliban figures where the opium economy is named as a FUNDING source in the listing narrative, not as the designation basis. Adding it to a narcotics + TCO tab would contribute ~12 relevant rows while importing 1,000 terrorism designations that dilute the focus. Same call as unodc-ids and opensanctions: a documented dead end, not a pending build. The genuine second-authority gap remains open — EU Sanctions Map is the better candidate.
sources.transform: none — revisit only if a narcotics-specific UN regime is ever created.

sources.name: OpenSanctions — consolidated global sanctions aggregate
sources.license: UNSTATED on the bulk artifacts — checked 2026-07-26, the dataset index returns null for both `license` and `license_url`
sources.feeds: REFERENCE LOOKUP ONLY, DELIBERATELY NOT BUNDLED. Aggregates OFAC/UN/EU and ~430 other lists more conveniently than fetching each, but shipping it in an MIT repo without a stated licence would be the same trap as other unstated-licence data sources. Use it to look an entity up; take the authoritative row from the issuing authority.
sources.transform: none — do not bundle without written licence confirmation

sources.name: EU Sanctions Map
sources.feeds: NOT YET INTEGRATED — third designating authority for the designation layer, with alias cross-references.

sources._section: INVESTIGATIVE REPORTS AND ANALYSIS — these are REPORTS, not datasets. They publish allegations, attributions and named individuals who are frequently NOT officially designated. They feed the governed scraper's analyst work queue (scripts/scrape/) as leads requiring verification, and must never be ingested into a bundled dataset the app renders as fact. Treating a report as a dataset is how an observatory ends up publishing an accusation as a statistic.

sources.name: DEA National Drug Threat Assessment
sources.feeds: Analyst context: Chinese precursor supply chains, cartel synthesis, fentanyl analogue flows. Corridor rows extractable to the flows CSV schema where DEA states an explicit origin/destination.
sources.transform: scripts/convert/from-pdf.mjs, corridor rows via the flows schema

sources.name: HIDTA regional Drug Threat Assessments
sources.feeds: Sub-national US detail, often more granular than the national NDTA. Note the grain guard: NarcoScope publishes state level at finest for the US, never county or city.

sources.name: UNODC Global SMART Programme — synthetic drugs & precursors
sources.feeds: Precursor and NPS monitoring; complements the INCB precursors report already ingested into FLOW_RECORDS.

sources.name: C4ADS — open-source investigations into illicit networks
sources.feeds: WORK QUEUE ONLY. Names Chinese precursor exporters and platform listings. Company names appearing here are allegations unless the entity also appears in ofac-sdn — cross-check before any row leaves the queue.
sources.transform: scripts/scrape/ (governed scraper) -> analyst verification -> only then a CSV row

sources.name: InSight Crime — investigative journalism on organised crime
sources.feeds: WORK QUEUE ONLY. Strongest on Latin American networks. Same rule as C4ADS: journalism is a lead, not a record.

sources.name: OCCRP Aleph — leaks, corporate registries, court records
sources.license: varies per collection; many require an account and carry redistribution restrictions
sources.feeds: REFERENCE LOOKUP ONLY. Excellent for resolving a corporate trail behind a designated entity. Nothing from Aleph may be bundled — collection licences vary and several forbid redistribution outright.

sources.name: RAND Drug Policy Research Center
sources.feeds: Methodology reference for supply-side economics, especially fentanyl market modelling. Read for method, cite for context; not a data feed.

sources.name: Stimson Center — Southeast Asia / Mekong programme
sources.feeds: Context on Chinese regulatory gaps and Mekong governance. Analysis, not data.

sources.name: Global Financial Integrity — illicit financial flows
sources.feeds: Trade-misinvoicing and illicit-flow estimates. Candidate input if a financial-flows layer is ever built; see docs/ROADMAP-PARALLEL-ECONOMY.md.

sources.name: The Sentry — war-economy financial investigations
sources.feeds: WORK QUEUE ONLY. Strong on military business empires and their banking relationships.

sources.name: Global Witness — resource, wildlife and corruption investigations
sources.feeds: WORK QUEUE ONLY. Covers the wildlife/timber/drug convergence in Southeast Asia.

sources.name: Fortify Rights — Myanmar human-rights documentation
sources.feeds: WORK QUEUE ONLY. Military-militia linkage documentation for the Myanmar conflict layer.

sources.name: CITES Trade Database — confiscations (Source='I')
sources.format: zip of ~59 CSV shards (~460 MB download, ~4.5 GB unzipped)
sources.cadence: annual (CITES releases a new database version each year; reporting lags ~2 years)
sources.license: CITES / UNEP-WCMC, attribution; free for non-commercial use
sources.feeds: src/data/wildlifeSeizures.json (Wildlife Seizures tab) — INTEGRATED 2026-07-27: 232,208 confiscation records 1977-2023, aggregated by class/taxon/country/year/term. NOT collector-automated: the 460 MB download is too heavy for the daily pipeline and the data is annual, so this is a one-time manual rebuild per CITES release.

sources.name: TRAFFIC — wildlife trade monitoring network
sources.feeds: WORK QUEUE ONLY (qualitative). The quantitative wildlife-seizure data now comes from cites-wildlife above; TRAFFIC's investigative reports remain leads for the analyst queue, documenting the SEZ convergence (Kings Romans, Mongla) narratively.

sources.name: Environmental Investigation Agency
sources.feeds: WORK QUEUE ONLY. Undercover investigations naming traders and market operators — the highest-allegation-density source in this registry, and correspondingly the one whose rows must never leave the queue unverified.

sources.name: Conflict Armament Research — weapon tracing
sources.feeds: Serial-number-level weapon tracing, including Myanmar. Arms flows are out of NarcoScope's scope; registered for the convergence picture.

sources.name: Small Arms Survey
sources.feeds: Illicit arms flow estimates. Same scope note as CAR.

sources.name: UN reporting on Myanmar (Special Rapporteur / OHCHR)
sources.feeds: Named arms deals, brokers and transport networks with evidentiary backing — UN documents are official records rather than journalism, so rows sourced here carry a higher reliability tier.

sources.name: Global Anti-Scam Organization — crowd-sourced scam-operation reports
sources.feeds: WORK QUEUE ONLY, LOWEST TIER. Entries are self-reported, unverified, and frequently name private individuals and specific compound locations. Graded 'low' in src/lib/sourceReliability.ts on purpose and must never be promoted. Useful for establishing that a phenomenon exists in a place; never sufficient to attribute it to a person.
